entities.summary:
Hegias of Athens was a renowned sculptor of the Late Archaic school in ancient Greece, active during the 6th century BCE. He is best known for his association with the famous sculptor Pheidias, and his work is believed to have influenced the development of Greek art during this period.

Born into a family of modest means, Hegias received training in the arts from the renowned sculptor Phidias, who would later become his mentor. Hegias' own style was characterized by its balance and harmony, and he is believed to have worked on several notable projects, including the statue of Pyrrhus supported by Pallas Athena.

Despite his significant contributions to Greek art, Hegias' work has largely been lost to time, and only a few fragmentary remains of his sculptures have survived. Nevertheless, his legacy as a sculptor of the Late Archaic school continues to be celebrated by art historians and enthusiasts alike.

The significance of Hegias' work extends beyond his artistic achievements, as it reflects the cultural and political climate of ancient Greece during the 6th century BCE. His sculptures, in particular, provide valuable insights into the values and beliefs of the ancient Greeks, and have helped to shape our understanding of this pivotal period in human history.

Hegias' impact on the development of Greek art cannot be overstated. His association with Pheidias, and his own contributions to the art of the Late Archaic school, helped to shape the course of artistic expression in ancient Greece. His work continues to inspire artists and art historians to this day, and his legacy serves as a testament to the enduring power of art to transcend time and culture.
